amends: v1.1 base plan; independent of v1.2 (identity) and v1.3 (reranker)

why_v14_was_superseded.fixed_k_volume_bias: v1.4 §4 mandated scoring the child, never the parent. That prevented parent-dilution and in the same stroke created its mirror: at fixed k a 128-token child retrieves ~6x less text than a 768-token parent (5x128=640 vs 5x768=3840). Measured Track A C0: parents@5 0.790 vs children@5 0.4886. H7 as written would have returned REJECT_HARM on both tracks for a MEASUREMENT-DESIGN reason, indistinguishable in the write-up from real harm.
why_v14_was_superseded.headroom_invalidated_by_the_fix: Scoring the delivered parent with a set-identical inventory means the treatment can only REORDER units, never surface new ones. v1.4 §2's ceiling-gap justification (1 - r@10) was therefore wrong; §2 is rewritten around r@inf - r@5.
why_v14_was_superseded.c4_provenance: Formatter units carry merged, disjoint sentence ranges spanning MORE original text than the unit's own text (one C4 unit: 108 ranges, span 7492 chars vs text 5371), over edited text whose offsets are not linear. ProvenanceNotDerivable is raised rather than guessed; the alternatives were handing children the parent's ranges (the dilution defect itself) or interpolating across edited text (fabricated provenance).

axis: orthogonal retrieval-unit change; every condition scored with and without small-to-big over the same corpus and query set, paired per query. NOT a new condition.
decides_on: Track B (150 queries, all test — dev_fraction 0.0). Track A (176 test queries) secondary no-harm check.

conditions_excluded.C1: semantic chunker already sets its own boundaries

headroom_bound.why_r10_minus_r5_is_WRONG: It measures reordering within an existing shortlist, which would be right only if best-child scoring were a local re-rank. Under max-over-children a parent whose whole-unit embedding is diluted — one relevant passage averaged with ~700 unrelated tokens — can sit at rank 200 under whole-unit scoring and rank 3 under best-child scoring, because the child carrying that passage is embedded alone. Nothing confines the movement to the top-10. That dilution-rescue IS the mechanism.
headroom_bound.recall_inf_definition: COVERAGE — the fraction of queries whose gold lies in SOME indexed unit. Computed without retrieval by checking every unit against every gold span, so it is exact rather than estimated.
headroom_bound.recall_inf_is_also_diagnostic: recall@inf < 1 for a condition means that condition's pipeline loses gold OUTRIGHT at any k. C4 is the one to watch: if a gold span sits in a duplicate whose ranges were not absorbed into the canonical unit it is unreachable at any k — a genuine treatment defect, invisible in every number reported to date.
headroom_bound.caveat_not_a_prediction: The realistically achievable fraction is a small share of the bound on both tracks. A large pool means the test is CAPABLE of expressing an outcome, not that one is expected.
headroom_bound.caveat_track_level_only: Per-condition pools inside a track are within noise at n=176/150. The bound scopes the primary hypothesis to a TRACK; it must NOT be used to drop or select conditions.
headroom_bound.data_source: v1.3 TEST artifacts extended in k, using run.py's --no-sweep configuration verbatim.
headroom_bound.admissibility_principle: Quantities that BOUND what an experiment could show are admissible pre-data; quantities that INDICATE what it would show are not. A headroom analysis can only shrink or cancel an experiment, never manufacture a positive — that asymmetry is what makes it safe on spent test data. Precedent: v1.4 §2's ceiling-gap table came from the same source and was approved in writing.
headroom_bound.measured_source: scripts/headroom_bound.py; v1.3 test artifacts extended in k; bge-base; run.py --no-sweep baseline config verbatim. Every r@5 and r@10 reproduces v1.3's published values exactly.
headroom_bound.conclusion: Track B pool is ~3-4x Track A's (+0.600..+0.647 vs +0.148..+0.210), so scoping H7 to Track B survives the correction on corrected reasoning.
headroom_bound.coverage_result: recall@inf = 1.000 on EVERY condition of BOTH tracks, including C4. The C4 gold-loss risk is RETIRED with evidence: dedup orphans no gold span on either corpus.
headroom_bound.spread_reading: Track A: r@50 already 0.972-0.989, so nearly the whole pool sits within the top 50 — short reordering distance. Track B: r@50 0.693-0.740 vs r@inf 1.000, so ~26-30 points of the pool lie BEYOND rank 50 — a larger pool that must also be moved further, reachable only by the dilution-rescue mechanism.
headroom_bound.limitation_a_coverage_near_tautological: For C0/C2 complete coverage is expected BY CONSTRUCTION (contiguous chunking + 'any' overlap), so the bound collapses to 1 - r@5 there. The measurement was still worth taking because it was the only way to find out whether C4 was the exception; C4 is the informative result.
headroom_bound.limitation_b_what_coverage_does_not_reti: Coverage is measured against a unit's CLAIMED ranges, and a C4 unit's ranges are wider than its own text (canonical absorbs duplicates' ranges: 108 ranges / 7492 chars vs 5371 chars of text). RETIRED: no gold span falls outside the union of claimed ranges. NOT RETIRED: no gold text was removed by dedup. These coincide only if absorbed duplicates were genuine duplicates — recorded as an explicit assumption.

child_construction_ONE_RULE_ALL_CONDITIO.rule: Split the condition's indexed text into sentences; greedily accumulate sentences into a child until adding the next would exceed child_tokens; emit. A sentence longer than child_tokens alone is hard-cut at a token boundary.
child_construction_ONE_RULE_ALL_CONDITIO.child_tokens_is_a_ceiling_not_a_size: Conditions will not land on identical distributions. Report realized child token distribution (mean, median, p10/p90) per condition.
child_construction_ONE_RULE_ALL_CONDITIO.why_uniform: Child cutting quality drives ranking quality, so condition-asymmetric cutting would be a machinery advantage in the one place that determines the entire result. One rule across three corpora, so the only thing differing between conditions is THE CORPUS, not the machinery.
child_construction_ONE_RULE_ALL_CONDITIO.sentence_alignment_re_decided_not_inheri: Originally adopted to give C4 derivable child provenance. Children now only RANK and are never scored, so that necessity evaporated. Kept on the independent uniformity ground above. Recorded as re-made rather than carried forward, because superseded requirements surviving as unexplained design is its own failure mode.
child_construction_ONE_RULE_ALL_CONDITIO.C2_children: blurb + child text; child_tokens is the ceiling on the child TEXT, blurb prepended on top. Faithful to what contextual retrieval does (context on every indexed unit) and keeps C2's child text directly comparable to C0's. Children rank only, so child size carries no volume consequence. Report mean blurb-to-child token ratio per track as the dilution diagnostic.

parents_set_identical_to_baseline_invent.C0: enclosing 768-token naive chunk = C0's baseline unit
parents_set_identical_to_baseline_invent.C2: enclosing naive chunk + blurb = C2's baseline unit
parents_set_identical_to_baseline_invent.C4: enclosing 768-token cut of formatted text = C4's baseline unit
parents_set_identical_to_baseline_invent.C4_marked_section_parents: DECLARED SECONDARY ARM, reported separately with the width asymmetry restated. Moving C4's primary parent to its baseline unit removes the last machinery asymmetry from the primary.

scoring.ranking: parents-ranked-by-best-child: each parent scored as max over its children, parents ranked by that score, top-k parents taken and delivered.
scoring.why_not_children_then_collapse: That makes the delivered ordering a function of the child pool size, which is a harness parameter rather than a property of the method.
scoring.hits_scored_on: the delivered PARENT. Parents are baseline units, so this is exactly what the baseline scores — same inventory, same widths, same delivered volume, different ranking function.
scoring.report_children_per_parent_distribution: max over N gives a parent with more children more chances at a high score. Parents are fixed-size baseline units so it should be near-uniform — but 'should be' is what the distribution is for.

guard.assertion: Set-identity between the s2b parent inventory and the baseline unit inventory, per condition per track — exact identity, not overlap or containment — checked at build time and again at scoring time.
guard.why_stronger_than_the_v14_invariance_tes: Widening becomes UNAVAILABLE rather than merely discouraged: any parent that is not literally a baseline unit fails the assertion.
guard.regression_guard_not_evidence: This assertion is TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION (parents are built from baseline units) and can only fail if a later refactor breaks the construction. Per template §A1b it is labelled a regression guard, and a negative control asserts it FAILS against a deliberately widened inventory.
guard.quantified_motivation: The v1.4 parent-dilution negative control measured recall@5 inflating by +0.267 (C0) and +0.301 (C2) on Track A — larger than any genuine effect in this programme. That is the documented reason for pinning the inventory rather than merely testing it.

hypotheses.H7: primary, Track B: for each X in {C0,C2,C4}, ranking X's units by best-child score improves recall@5 (hybrid, 'any') over ranking them by whole-unit score, paired over queries, at child_tokens=128
hypotheses.H7a: secondary, Track A: no-harm check — best-child ranking does not significantly REDUCE recall@5
hypotheses.H7b: robustness: H7 at child_tokens=256, reported alongside 128, no post-hoc selection
hypotheses.H7c: descriptive, NO decision weight: localisation precision at fixed k (child-scored); realized child token distributions; children-per-parent distribution; blurb-to-child ratio

H7c_caption_note: For C4 a sentence range is PROVENANCE OF ORIGIN, not byte-identity — the formatter may have edited the sentence, so the range identifies where the text came from rather than asserting the text is verbatim.

decision_arithmetic.form_chosen: per-condition, NOT pooled. C0/C2/C4 are different corpora, not replicates, so a pooled delta is not a well-defined single effect and would let a harm in one condition be averaged away by gains in another.
decision_arithmetic.significant_definition: paired CI excludes 0 after Holm within {C0,C2,C4}, positive direction
decision_arithmetic.passing_conditions_in_a_KILL_pattern: recorded as hypotheses for a future pre-registered test, never as a verdict
decision_arithmetic.child_size_scope: if 128 yields KILL AND 256 would independently yield ADOPT, the verdict is ADOPT_SCOPED — child size ('helps at 256, not at 128'). No other child-size pattern creates a scope.
decision_arithmetic.precedence: REJECT_HARM overrides every row, including a full ADOPT sweep.

multiplicity_across_child_size.decision: Holm over ALL SIX tests (three conditions x two child sizes) as a SINGLE family.
multiplicity_across_child_size.rejected_alternative: two families plus an honest 'rests on an uncorrected second look' label
multiplicity_across_child_size.why: Removes the multiplicity rather than annotating it. Two child sizes otherwise give two looks at a positive verdict with an uncontrolled family-wise error rate across the size axis. The cost is a higher bar, which is the correct direction for a claim that would otherwise rest on two looks, and it makes a child-size scope a FINDING rather than a caveated one. Holm is valid under arbitrary dependence, so the two sizes sharing corpora and queries is not an obstacle.
multiplicity_across_child_size.accepted_consequence: With six comparisons the correction is stricter, so a genuine but small effect is more likely to be missed. Traded deliberately.

decision_rules.ADOPT: all three of {C0,C2,C4} individually significant positive on Track B at child_tokens=128 after Holm, AND H7a clean (no significant harm on Track A)
decision_rules.ADOPT_SCOPED: significant-positive set exactly matches a pre-named family, or the child-size scope. Any other pattern is KILL, not a scope
decision_rules.KILL: no significant positive, or a set not exactly matching a pre-named family
decision_rules.REJECT_HARM: significant NEGATIVE on any primary condition on EITHER track — same rule as ADOPT, sign reversed

branch_precedence: REJECT_HARM takes precedence over every other branch; a harm finding is reported as harm, never as a null and never offset by gains elsewhere
mandatory_verdict_wording: If the verdict is ADOPT_SCOPED — formatted family {C4}, the §5 secondary-arm asymmetry MUST be restated in the verdict text itself, so 'small-to-big helps only on formatted corpora' cannot silently absorb 'C4's parents are denser by treatment'.
holm_families: H7's three Track B conditions form one family. Track A no-harm checks form a SEPARATE family. Neither merges with v1.1's H1-H4 or v1.3's H6. Child-size variants reported separately, never pooled.
one_shot_rule: If H7 fails, changing child size, parent definition, ranking function or embedder and re-testing on this same Track A/B split is NOT a fresh test; a retry needs a new pre-registered amendment.
reporting_rule: H7c and any interaction are reported in whichever direction they fall; a result unfavourable to small-to-big or to the formatter is reported with equal prominence.

residual_asymmetry.primary: NONE. Children sentence-aligned everywhere and C4's primary parent width-matched to its baseline unit; the only differences between conditions are the corpora.
residual_asymmetry.secondary_arm_only: marked-section parents are semantically coherent and variable-width against C0/C2's fixed windows; reported separately with the asymmetry restated at the point of comparison.
residual_asymmetry.treatment_effect_declared_up_front: C4's parents hold denser text (dedup removed redundancy), so its children may be more heterogeneous and its max correspondingly higher. Treatment effect, not artifact — stated here rather than discovered in the results.
residual_asymmetry.c4_density_is_a_HYPOTHESIS_not_a_fact: Unit counts weakly contradict the density claim: Track A C0 90 vs C4 90; Track B C0 378 vs C4 379. If dedup had removed material redundancy the formatted corpus would cut into fewer 768-token units. Reference resolution and right-sizing plausibly add back what dedup removes. §7's mandatory verdict wording must NOT lean on density as established; to be settled by the realized child token distributions and unit counts, reported either way.

environment_pins.baseline_config: run.py --no-sweep verbatim: C0 {chunk_tokens 768, overlap_frac 0.0}; C2 and C4 take YAML defaults. A first headroom pass that overrode only chunk_tokens measured a DIFFERENT C0 (91 units, r@5 0.722) than v1.3 ran (90 units, r@5 0.790).
environment_pins.comparability_note: v1.5 absolutes are comparable to v1.3's, NEVER to v1.1's (MiniLM stack). Only within-run paired deltas travel across amendments.
environment_pins.truncation_note: v1.3's confound does not apply — no cross-encoder here, and 128/256-token children sit inside bge-base's 512-token input window, so no indexed text is truncated before embedding.

child_size_cost_decision.decision: BOTH child sizes (128 and 256) will be run. Neither is dropped.
child_size_cost_decision.if_a_cut_becomes_necessary: documented amendment recorded BEFORE any child_tokens=128 result exists, stating compute cost as the reason. Running both and reporting the better one — or skipping 256 'for time' after seeing 128 — is indistinguishable from post-hoc selection after the fact.

calibration_data_declaration: The parents@5 0.790 / children@5 0.4886 calibration was measured on Track A TEST. It is a property of the BASELINE CONFIGURATION (the token volume a fixed k delivers), not a treatment outcome, and it motivated a measurement-validity repair rather than a hypothesis fitted to an observed result. From here calibration runs on Track A DEV only, never Track B (dev_fraction 0.0 — every query is test on the primary track).

retrieval_specification.both_arms_identical_depth_and_fusion_loc: For each modality independently: rank children, walk the ranked child list emitting each parent on FIRST APPEARANCE until index.candidate_pool DISTINCT parents are emitted or the child list is exhausted (first appearance IS max-over-children). Then RRF-fuse the two PARENT-level rankings with the same k_rrf and take top-k parents.
retrieval_specification.pool_denomination: candidate_pool is denominated in DELIVERED PARENTS in both arms, never in indexed children. The child-side pool is whatever depth reaches that many distinct parents — variable per query, which is correct: the child side is the harness parameter, the delivered side is pinned.
retrieval_specification.why: Handing children to Retriever caused two one-directional biases against the treatment, both in the primary metric: (1) fusion at CHILD level loses RRF's cross-modality agreement bonus, so the treatment behaves like max(dense,sparse) while the baseline behaves like dense+sparse — changing the ranking function AND the fusion locus at once; (2) 50 children is bounded above by 50 parents and in practice fewer, truncating the deep-reordering reach that §2 identifies as the source of Track B's entire advantage.
retrieval_specification.baseline_untouched: so v1.3's published values still reproduce exactly and §2's configuration-match check survives
retrieval_specification.depth_assertion: both arms' per-modality parent rankings must have equal length per query (both reached candidate_pool, or both exhausted). Negative control asserts ParentRankingDepthMismatch fires when the walk is truncated in children rather than parents.

parentcontext_scope_under_v15: The primary parent IS a baseline Unit and carries source_ranges legitimately, because the pinned inventory means no wider parent is reachable. The v1.4 type separation RETIRES from the primary path and survives only for the C4 marked-section secondary arm, where parents are not baseline units and dilution is still live.
